text:
julian: hi! new engineer here. trying to onboard my service and need a secrets workflow. question: should I create a service account + Vault role or request direct kv write perms for my app path?

li: welcome :wave: best practice is service account -> short-lived role. create a cloud service account (GCP/AWS) and we map it to a Vault role via the auth backend. avoids long-lived tokens.

julian: ok. how do i request the mapping? any boilerplate?

li: open the Access form: https://redwood.internal/selfservice -> Access: Vault -> choose "service-account to role". attach the service account email and the app repo name. include the desired secret path (e.g., secret/data/services/metrics-service).

ops-rotation: FYI for production we use policies named `svc-read-<team>` or `svc-readwrite-<team>`. rotation cadence depends on type: API keys rotate 90d, CI tokens 30d, and service account wrappers are rotated on role rebinds.

julian: can I provision secrets via Terraform during deploy?

li: yes — we use the hashicorp/vault provider in infra repo. example snippet we use in infra/templates:
```
resource "vault_kv_secret_v2" "svc_api_key" {
  mount = "secret"
  name  = "services/metrics-service"
  data_json = jsonencode({ api_key = var.api_key })
}
```
Make sure the pipeline uses a `vault` CI role with `write` to that path.

julian: where does KMS come in? do we store raw KMS keys in Vault?

ops-rotation: we don't store raw root keys in Vault. For envelope encryption we keep KMS keys in cloud KMS and store wrapped blobs in Vault. We also use the `transit` engine for signing/encryption ops, backed by a KMS-wrapped root key in the operator account.

julian: got it. what's the manual process if i need a one-off secret during onboarding?

li: create a ticket via the form and request `temp-write` on the specific path. devex can issue a short-lived policy for up to 8 hours for onboarding tasks. include justification and expiry in the ticket.

devex-bot: Ticket created #VAULT-4999 for julian 6 ops team review. Reminder: include repo link and CI pipeline ID.

julian: thanks! last q: how are rotations audited?

ops-rotation: all writes/versions in KV v2 are time-stamped and captured. rotation service emits events to Kafka and we keep an audit log in GCS for 90 days. ops team can trigger emergency rollouts via the rotation tool at https://redwood.internal/ops/rotate.

julian: perfect, that's everything for now. i'll open the form and attach infra PR. thanks :thumbsup:
